blocks.content: • Sea Cliffs – steep rock faces formed by wave attack.
• Wave-Cut Platform – flat rocky surface at base of cliffs.
• Sea Caves – hollow openings created by hydraulic action.
• Sea Arches – formed when caves enlarge and meet.
Differential erosion causes hard rocks to form headlands while softer rocks form bays.
• Stacks – isolated pillars formed after arch collapse.
• Blowholes – vertical shafts formed when caves extend upward.
• Headlands – resistant rocks projecting into sea.
• Bays – recessed coastal areas formed in softer rocks.

items: Remember the correct sequence of evolution: Sea Cave → Sea Arch → Stack → Stump.
Hydraulic action specifically forms sea caves, whereas wave attack forms steep sea cliffs.
Headlands consist of resistant (hard) rocks, while Bays are formed in softer rocks due to differential erosion.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Sea cliffs are steep rock faces formed by wave attack, leaving a flat rocky surface known as a wave-cut platform at their base.
Hydraulic action forms sea caves, which can enlarge and meet to form sea arches.
When a sea arch collapses, it leaves isolated pillars called stacks, which further erode into stumps.
Blowholes are vertical shafts created when caves extend upward to the ground surface.
Differential erosion shapes the shoreline by forming headlands from resistant rock and bays from softer rock.

blocks.content: Differential erosion causes hard rocks to form headlands while softer rocks form bays.
